answer.answer: The evidence is pinned to Early Access Update 1 through Hotfix 0.2.8 (Steam build 23761620, released 2026-06-17), SRDB 2.3.4 captured 2026-07-11, and a strongly corroborated—but unofficial—54-minute community/game-data cycle model. Mission Timeline is the selected design; historical evidence does not prove simulator or installation readiness. The proposed Watch Session presents Fire wave, Cooling, Recovery, World active, and Ruptura warning, with an across-the-room hero countdown targeting the next meaningful event—ordinary Vermin return during recovery, otherwise warning/Ruptura. Opportunities are independent versioned records with provenance and caveats, never automatic phase consequences or guarantees of safety. An honest native MVP uses explicit confidence states, separate accessible alert signatures, absolute-date notifications, deduplication and resume reconciliation, a Live Activity only for the armed event, deliberate AlarmKit arming, visible capability status, and no Critical Alerts or background guarantees.

claims.value: The design evidence is pinned to Early Access Update 1 through Hotfix 0.2.8, Steam build 23761620 released 2026-06-17, plus SRDB 2.3.4 captured 2026-07-11. Its 54-minute local-impact-to-impact cycle is a versioned community/game-data model, not an official eternal formula. Mission Timeline was selected on 2026-07-11, but that historical record explicitly lacks proof that simulator and phone-install acceptance passed; current repository readiness remains unverified here.
source_paths: Projects/RuptureOps/Rupture cycle timer - research and product design.md

claims.value: The proposed player timeline is Fire wave 0:00–0:30, Cooling 0:30–1:30, Recovery/quiet window 1:30–11:30, World active 11:30–51:30, and Ruptura warning 51:30–54:00. The portrait hierarchy is: sync/capability status; semantic state plus huge countdown; threat instruction; at most two opportunity cards; then next events and safe controls. During recovery the hero counts down until ordinary Vermin are expected to return; otherwise it targets the next warning or Ruptura. A proportional overview may remain, but minimum-width labels or an event list must keep short phases visible, and color cannot be the only signal.
source_paths: Projects/RuptureOps/Rupture cycle timer - research and product design.md

claims.value: Each opportunity is proposed as independently versioned data containing its start/end event or offset, action, caveat, evidence class, confidence, applicable game build, and source snapshot. Recovery means lower ambient threat—not guaranteed safety—and triggered Geo Scanner, monolith, infection, Base Core, scripted POI, or variable-spawn behavior may disagree. Enemy-return and gathering windows must remain separate from phase mechanics so later validation can move them without rewriting the cycle model; unvalidated opportunities stay experimental or hidden.
source_paths: Projects/RuptureOps/Rupture cycle timer - research and product design.md

claims.value: The MVP proposal requires distinct enemy-return and Ruptura sounds and haptics plus persistent visual/text signals; it must never rely on color or audio alone or replay a backlog of missed cues after resume. Confidence is explicit—Unsynced, Manual sync - predicted, Confirmed at one later transition, Drift suspected, or Cycle data changed - re-sync required—and is downgraded after corrections, clock/model changes, uncertain pauses, save/reload, or server stops; no numerical accuracy is claimed before measurement. Native behavior uses absolute-date local notifications rescheduled after model/anchor changes, cycle-plus-event deduplication, resume recomputation, visible permission/capability status, and a Live Activity only for the currently armed event. AlarmKit is an iOS 26 opt-in enhancement requiring deliberate arming; earlier systems use normal notifications, Time Sensitive is separately optional, Critical Alerts are inappropriate, and the screen-awake controller restores the idle-timer setting when released.
source_paths: Projects/RuptureOps/Rupture cycle timer - research and product design.md

claims.value: Enemy-return and Ruptura alerts require distinct sounds and haptics plus persistent text, symbols, and borders; cues must never depend on color or audio alone, replay missed backlogs, flash full-screen, or tick every second by default. Native iOS behavior schedules local notifications at absolute dates, recomputes from the anchor on resume, deduplicates by cycle and event, keeps one currently armed Live Activity, disables idle sleep only while the monitor is active, and never uses background audio as a keep-alive. AlarmKit is opt-in for a deliberately armed event or session; normal notifications are the fallback, and Critical Alerts are inappropriate.

claims.value: The recovered prior architecture is a distributed backbone-and-spurs factory with a protected hub, low-heat processing cells, mining outposts, single-item buffered rail lines, and measurement-driven trunk upgrades instead of a monolithic mega-base.

The superseding requirement is one Constructorizer plus two Facturers while every Base Core remains level 0: 500 + 650 + 650 = 1,800 total machine heat, versus 1,000 capacity per level-0 core; exceeding a core’s capacity disables Fire Wave protection.

The safe proposed layout uses three occupied level-0 cores: the Constructorizer alone at one core for 500 machine heat and 500 remaining headroom, and one Facturer alone at each of two other cores for 650 machine heat and 350 remaining headroom each. Constructorizer-plus-Facturer (1,150), two Facturers (1,300), and all three machines (1,800) are rejected as unsafe co-locations; support-building heat must also fit within each core’s remaining headroom.

No construction or live-load verification is complete. Before building, audit the three candidate Core panels and unlock menus, include every existing and planned support load in the per-core arithmetic, proceed only when each projected total is at most 1,000, and use only confirmed Update 1 content—excluding Rail v.4/v.5, hidden buildings, future/endgame content, and pre-Update-1 guidance.

answer.answer: Committed a buildable child checkpoint retaining the parent. The safe Update 1 proposal uses three separate level-0 cores: one Constructorizer core and two single-Facturer cores. Required machine heat is 1,800 total; every possible pair exceeds a core's 1,000 capacity, so no co-location is safe. Construction remains gated on confirming each core's complete projected load and current unlocks.

claims.value: Historical recovered state: the parent architecture replaced the monolithic mega-base with an Update 1-only distributed backbone-and-spurs network of modular processing cells and mining outposts.

Superseding requirement: operate one 500-heat Constructorizer and two 650-heat Facturers while every Base Core remains level 0; required heavy-machine heat is 500 + 650 + 650 = 1,800 against 1,000 capacity per core.

Proposed safe layout, not yet built or tested: use three distinct level-0 cores—Constructorizer alone at 500/1,000, leaving at most 500 for other loads, and one Facturer alone at each remaining core at 650/1,000, leaving at most 350 each. Constructorizer plus Facturer is 1,150, and two Facturers are 1,300, so every heavy-machine co-location is rejected.

Version-safe next action: before construction, verify three candidate Core panels, complete projected heat including existing and support buildings, available power, and current Update 1 unlocks; build one machine per core only where total load remains at most 1,000, excluding hidden, future, and pre-Update-1 equipment.

answer.answer: The prior distributed backbone-and-spurs plan remains valid, but the new requirement forces three occupied level-0 core districts. A Constructorizer is 500 heat and each Facturer is 650: together they total 1,800, while every possible heavy-machine pair is also unsafe at 1,150 or 1,300 against a 1,000-capacity core. Proposed layout: one Constructorizer core and two separate single-Facturer cores, with respective pre-support headroom of 500, 350, and 350. Count all supporting-building heat before construction, remain below 1,000 with margin, and use only verified Update 1 equipment.

next_actions.title: Before construction, inspect the save and record the Core panel/load and Update 1 build/unlock menu for three candidate cores; make a per-core heat ledger including existing and support loads.

Proceed only if the Constructorizer cell totals no more than 1,000 and each Facturer cell totals no more than 1,000; otherwise remove or relocate support load rather than co-locating heavy machines or relying on unverified amplifiers.

current_state: CURRENT FACT: Update 1 (0.2.x) is the governing version; hidden, future, and pre-Update-1 equipment is excluded.
CURRENT FACT: each level-0 Base Core has 1,000 heat capacity, and exceeding capacity disables Fire Wave protection.
CURRENT FACT: one Constructorizer is 500 heat and each Facturer is 650 heat, so the required heavy-machine load is 500 + 650 + 650 = 1,800 heat.

HISTORICAL EVIDENCE RETAINED: the prior checkpoint replaced a monolithic mega-base with a distributed backbone-and-spurs architecture using rail/power trunks, modular cells, and single-item lines/buffers.

PROPOSED SUPERSEDING STATE: use three separate occupied level-0 core cells connected by the Update 1 rail/power backbone: one Constructorizer-only core at 500 heavy-machine heat and two Facturer-only cores at 650 heavy-machine heat each; no construction or in-save verification has yet occurred.
decisions: Reject Constructorizer + Facturer co-location because 500 + 650 = 1,150 > 1,000, and reject two-Facturer co-location because 650 + 650 = 1,300 > 1,000; either arrangement would disable Fire Wave protection before ancillary loads.

Assign exactly one required heavy machine per occupied level-0 core. Reserve at most 500 heat for all existing/support buildings in the Constructorizer cell and at most 350 heat in each Facturer cell; these margins are local and cannot be pooled across cores.

Preserve the prior distributed backbone-and-spurs pattern and Update 1-only authority rules. Rail v.1/v.2/v.3 may be selected only when actually unlocked and justified by measured flow; exclude Rail v.4/v.5, hidden buildings, future content, and playtest-era guidance.

Treat the three-cell arrangement as a proposal, not a verified build. Construction is gated on a per-core heat ledger proving existing load + the assigned heavy machine + every required support building is no more than 1,000 at each occupied core.
next_actions: Before construction, inspect the save and record the Core panel/load and Update 1 build/unlock menu for three candidate cores; make a per-core heat ledger including existing and support loads.

Proceed only if the Constructorizer cell totals no more than 1,000 and each Facturer cell totals no more than 1,000; otherwise remove or relocate support load rather than co-locating heavy machines or relying on unverified amplifiers.

After the ledger passes, build the three isolated heavy-machine cells on the existing backbone-and-spurs network, then verify each Core panel still shows Fire Wave protection active before commissioning recipes.

answer.answer: Committed child checkpoint checkpoint:019f934e-0655-7241-83e2-78de605a6110, retaining parent checkpoint:019f930a354277629c0586c2cb81a205. The safe proposal uses three separate level-0 cores: one Constructorizer core at 500/1,000 heat and two Facturer cores at 650/1,000 each. Any heavy-machine co-location is unsafe. Construction remains gated on live per-site heat and power ledgers using Update 1-confirmed equipment only.

claims.value: The recovered prior architecture is a distributed backbone-and-spurs network with modular production cells and mining outposts; rails carry both items and power, replacing the superseded monolithic mega-base concept.

The superseding requirement is one Constructorizer and two Facturers while every Base Core stays level 0. Their machine heat is 500 + 650 + 650 = 1,800 total; a level-0 core holds 1,000, while Constructorizer+Facturer is 1,150 and Facturer+Facturer is 1,300, so every two-machine or three-machine co-location exceeds capacity and would disable Fire Wave protection.

The safe proposed layout assigns each heavy machine to a distinct level-0 core: Constructorizer at 500/1,000 with 500 headroom, Facturer A at 650/1,000 with 350 headroom, and Facturer B at 650/1,000 with 350 headroom. Existing and support-building heat must fit within each site's remaining headroom; the layout has not yet been built or validated in the save.

Before construction, record live heat and power ledgers for three candidate cores and confirm each site's existing load plus its assigned machine and support load is at most 1,000. Then build one site at a time and recheck Fire Wave protection, using only Update 1-confirmed equipment; hidden content, Rail v.4/v.5, and pre-Update-1 guidance remain excluded.

checkpoint.objective: Operate one Constructorizer and two Facturers across level-0 Base Cores while preserving Fire Wave protection and Update 1 authority.
current_state: Authoritative capacity is 1,000 heat per level-0 core; Constructorizer heat is 500 and Facturer heat is 650.
The required machines total 1,800 heat across the network, but capacity is enforced per core.
The proposed three-core allocation is arithmetically safe for the heavy machines alone; live support loads and power provisioning remain unverified.
decisions: Retain the distributed backbone-and-spurs architecture.
Reject every co-location of the required heavy machines.
Allocate one Constructorizer and one Facturer each to three distinct level-0 cores.
Do not rely on disputed amplifier values or any hidden, future, or pre-Update-1 equipment.

Build and energize one site at a time, checking the Core panel and Fire Wave protection after each placement.
Relocate support loads or select another level-0 core whenever a site fails its gate.

gates.title: Every Base Core remains level 0.

Each occupied core's measured total heat, including existing and support buildings, is at most 1,000 before and after construction.
Fire Wave protection remains enabled at every occupied core.

goals.title: Revise the Update 1 distributed-factory plan into a buildable level-0 layout operating one Constructorizer and two Facturers while preserving Fire Wave protection at every occupied Base Core.

next_actions.title: Before construction, inspect the live Update 1 build/unlock menu and record a heat-and-power ledger for three candidate level-0 cores.

Reserve one candidate core for the Constructorizer and one separate candidate core for each Facturer. For each site, gate construction on measured existing heat + assigned machine heat + confirmed support heat being at most 1,000; if a gate fails, relocate support or choose another level-0 core.

After all three ledgers pass, build and energize one site at a time, rechecking the Core panel and Fire Wave protection after each placement; stop and roll back that placement if total heat exceeds 1,000.
Use only confirmed Update 1 rail and power components, beginning with Rail v.1 and upgrading to v.2/v.3 only when measured throughput requires it.

RECOVERED PRIOR ARCHITECTURE: the superseded monolithic mega-base was already replaced by an Update 1 backbone-and-spurs distributed network with a protected hub, modular low-heat cells, and mining spurs/outposts; rails carry both items and power, and Update 1 rail tiers are v.1/v.2/v.3.

RECOMPUTED CONSTRAINT: the three required heavy machines total 1,800 heat. Constructorizer plus Facturer is 1,150; two Facturers are 1,300; all three are 1,800. Each combination exceeds one level-0 core's 1,000 capacity, so every heavy-machine co-location is rejected.

Existing and support-building heat must fit inside that site's remaining headroom; otherwise relocate support to another level-0 core rather than co-locating heavy machines.
decisions: Retain the distributed backbone-and-spurs architecture and connect the three machine sites with only confirmed Update 1 equipment; Rail v.1/v.2/v.3 are allowed as throughput requires, while v.4/v.5, hidden buildings, and pre-Update-1 guidance remain excluded.
Reject Constructorizer+Facturer, Facturer+Facturer, and all-three co-location at any level-0 core because their machine heat alone exceeds 1,000.

Build only after a per-site heat ledger proves current load plus the assigned machine plus all local support heat is at most 1,000; preserve extra margin where practicable.

claims.value: Straylight is an agent-first, user-owned portable context and durable-work layer that preserves learned knowledge plus live resumable work state—including evidence, decisions, plans, artifacts, computations, checkpoints, and next actions—while Obsidian and Markdown remain prototype inputs, projections, and export formats rather than the canonical product boundary.

Historically, retrieval policy 0.2 passed 17 of 20 cases, recovered 46 of 53 evidence items, used 2,932 mean estimated tokens, and kept P95 context at 11,999 characters; one-shot top-k also passed 17 of 20, recovered 48 of 53, and used about 1,070 mean estimated tokens. These retrieval-only token estimates did not validate the workspace hypothesis or measure the new persistent API: they establish a regression baseline, while cumulative cached replay and uncached input must now be measured separately.

The mandated but not yet verified first persistent build slice is a typed, snapshot-pinned reopen-refresh-query/read-checkpoint path: reopen a parent checkpoint at revision N, refresh to N+1 with an explicit diff, combine exact and lexical retrieval with a pluggable semantic path, batch queries and reads, and commit an immutable child retaining parent and source references without reconstructing the complete prior corpus when checkpoint plus delta suffice.

The measurable transition gate is to match direct-filesystem answer claims in no more than four completed workspace calls per case, demonstrate N-to-N+1 diff exposure and immutable parent-linked checkpoint lineage, preserve exact source references, avoid unnecessary full-corpus reconstruction, and report cumulative cached replay separately from uncached input. This gate is defined but has not yet been shown to pass.

claims.value: Straylight is a user-owned, portable agent context and durable-work layer that preserves learned knowledge and live work state so later agents can resume, inspect, revise, and advance complex work.

The completed retrieval evaluation did not demonstrate workspace token efficiency: policy 0.2's process-per-operation workspace passed 17 of 20 cases, recovered 46 of 53 evidence items, and used about 2,932 mean estimated tokens, while one-shot top-k also passed 17 of 20, recovered 48 of 53, and used about 1,070; these historical retrieval-only results are a regression baseline, not the current product or implementation gate.

The proposed first persistent build slice is a snapshot-pinned typed workspace that reopens a parent checkpoint at revision N, refreshes to N+1 with a visible diff, batches query and read operations, combines exact and lexical retrieval with a pluggable semantic path, and commits an immutable lineage-preserving child checkpoint without reconstructing the full corpus when checkpoint plus delta suffice; implementation is not yet verified.

The measurable transition gate requires each harness case to complete in no more than four workspace calls while matching the direct-filesystem answer claims, with cumulative cached replay and uncached input reported separately.

current_state: CURRENT FACT: Straylight is a user-owned, portable agent context and durable-work layer that preserves learned knowledge and live resumable work state.

SUPERSEDING STATE: Explicit project-owner direction advances Straylight from evaluation into implementation; the BM25 shell remains only a regression fixture.
INCOMPLETE WORK: The persistent API slice and transition harness have been specified but are not yet implemented or verified.
decisions: Build a persistent, snapshot-pinned workspace rather than extend the process-per-operation BM25 shell.

The first persistent slice will reopen a parent checkpoint at revision N, refresh to N+1 with an evidence/constraint diff, provide typed batched query/read operations combining exact and lexical retrieval with a pluggable semantic path, and commit an immutable lineage-preserving child checkpoint without reconstructing the full corpus when checkpoint plus delta suffice.

Accept the transition only when every harness case completes in no more than four workspace calls, its answer claims match the direct-filesystem condition, and cumulative cached replay and uncached input are reported separately.

claims.value: CURRENT FACT: Straylight is a user-owned, portable, agent-first context and durable-work layer that preserves learned knowledge together with the evidence, decisions, computations, artifacts, questions, checkpoints, and next actions needed to resume and advance complex work.

CORRECTED INTERPRETATION: The completed retrieval-only token result is historical efficiency evidence, not proof of product success; cumulative cached replay and uncached input must be reported separately, while retrieval-only performance remains a regression lane subordinate to continuation, source fidelity, verification, and durable-state quality.

DECIDED BUT NOT YET VERIFIED: The first persistent build slice reopens a revision-N parent checkpoint, refreshes it to N+1 while exposing the changed evidence or constraint as a diff, provides typed batched query/read operations with exact and lexical retrieval plus a pluggable semantic path, and commits an immutable source-preserving child without reconstructing the full prior corpus when checkpoint plus delta suffice.

UNMET TRANSITION GATE: Each case must match the direct-filesystem answer claims in no more than four completed workspace calls, preserve parent and prior-plus-delta source lineage in an immutable child checkpoint, and report cumulative cached replay separately from uncached input.

claims.value: Straylight is a user-owned, portable, agent-first context and durable-work layer that preserves learned knowledge and live resumable work state so later agents can inspect, revise, and advance complex work.

The completed retrieval-readiness benchmark is historical regression evidence, not proof of product success or holdout performance; token reporting must also distinguish cumulative cached replay from uncached input rather than treating them as one interchangeable result.

The proposed first persistent build slice reopens a parent checkpoint at revision N, refreshes to N+1 with an explicit diff, supports typed batched reads and queries using exact and lexical retrieval plus a pluggable semantic path, and commits an immutable child checkpoint with parent and source lineage without reconstructing the complete prior corpus.

The measurable transition gate is no more than four completed workspace calls per case while matching direct-filesystem answer claims, with cumulative cached replay and uncached input reported separately.

answer.answer: Straylight now moves from retrieval evaluation to a persistent, snapshot-pinned API implementation. The historical 1,070-versus-2,932 token figures measure estimated retrieval context, not verified API usage or cost. The first slice is the typed checkpoint/session spine, gated by claim parity, lineage preservation, separate token accounting, and no more than four workspace calls per case.

claims.value: Straylight is a user-owned, portable context and durable-work layer that lets agents learn, continue, and iteratively advance complex work without treating every transcript as permanent memory or collapsing distinct trust domains.

The historical retrieval-only evaluation reported about 1,070 mean estimated tokens for one-shot top-k versus 2,932 for the minimal workspace. These are estimated retrieval-context quantities, not verified end-to-end persistent-API token usage, latency, or cost; the new evaluation must report cumulative cached replay separately from uncached input.

The proposed first persistent build slice is a typed, snapshot-pinned session and checkpoint spine that reopens the revision-N parent, refreshes to N+1 with an evidence diff, batches exact and lexical retrieval plus a pluggable semantic path and source reads, and commits an immutable source-linked child without reconstructing the complete corpus.

The measurable transition gate requires each harness case to complete in no more than four workspace calls, match the direct-filesystem answer claims, preserve parent-checkpoint and source lineage, expose the N-to-N+1 delta, and report cumulative cached replay separately from uncached input.

answer.answer: Straylight now advances into implementation through a persistent, snapshot-pinned API workspace. The historical retrieval/token result remains regression evidence and cannot represent fresh per-call cost unless cached replay and uncached input are reported separately. The first slice and measurable transition gate are persisted in child checkpoint checkpoint:019f9351-e280-7202-86c8-738468ad0e8d.

claims.value: Straylight is a user-owned, portable, agent-first context and durable-work layer that preserves learned knowledge and live work state—including evidence, decisions, computations, checkpoints, and next actions—so later agents can inspect, resume, and advance complex work.

The completed retrieval-readiness benchmark is historical regression evidence, not proof of product success; a token result must not be interpreted as fresh per-call implementation cost unless cumulative cached replay and uncached input are reported separately.

The approved first build slice is a persistent, snapshot-pinned workspace that reopens a revision-N parent checkpoint, refreshes to N+1, exposes the delta, provides typed batched query/read using exact and lexical retrieval plus a pluggable semantic path, and commits an immutable source-preserving child checkpoint without reconstructing the complete prior corpus.

The transition passes when each case matches the direct-filesystem answer claims in no more than four completed workspace calls, exposes the N-to-N+1 diff, preserves parent and source lineage in an immutable child checkpoint, avoids unnecessary full-corpus reconstruction, and reports cumulative cached replay separately from uncached input; implementation remains incomplete until this harness passes.

decisions: Build the first vertical slice as a persistent snapshot-pinned workspace that reopens a revision-N parent checkpoint, refreshes to N+1, and exposes the changed evidence or constraint as a diff.

Provide typed batched query and read operations combining exact and lexical retrieval with a pluggable semantic retrieval path, then commit an immutable child checkpoint naming its parent and preserving source references.
Do not reconstruct the full prior corpus when the parent checkpoint and revision delta are sufficient.
Treat retrieval-only scores and BM25 behavior as regression evidence, not product acceptance.

PVE34 remains historical architecture evidence, while later adaptive-autonomy results remain the operating basis. The next trial is now a 30-minute dev-only alpha soak: batch starts with a 128 ceiling, fetch remains adaptive, production and durable persistence are untouched, and the trial advances to beta only after meeting the throughput, integrity, connection, and restart gates. Abort and roll back on any integrity, recovery, or protected-state violation, MySQL memory above 90% for two consecutive minutes, or more than three DB connection failures per minute.

claims.value: The recovered prior state retains PVE34 as verified historical evidence: it reached and validated 10.019M, with the final 200k crossing chunk averaging 403/sec steady and 408/sec late, demonstrating the split fetch/DB architecture and DB/write coordination bottleneck. Later adaptive-autonomy evidence superseded it as the performance baseline, including 1083.1 PGCR/sec average and 1122.9/sec steady on current-code alpha, while establishing adaptive fetch, reversible fixed-budget DB-lane trials, a batch-128 keeper ceiling, and restart recovery from DB truth.

claims.value: The new explicit operator constraint replaces the earlier open-ended longer-alpha proposal with a 30-minute dev-only alpha soak that cannot change production or add durable controller persistence. Acceptance requires at least 900 PGCR/sec steady throughput during the final 10 minutes, zero integrity or recovery violations, no DB connection failure storm, and a successful restart from DB truth after the controlled stop; rollback is required if MySQL exceeds 90% of host memory for two consecutive minutes or DB connection failures exceed three per minute.

The PVE34 and adaptive-autonomy notes remain historical and implementation evidence, whereas the new delta is authoritative only for the next experiment’s bounds and gates. It does not supersede the established integrity model: DB rows are truth, raw marker commits travel with summaries, failed rows retry immediately, availability failures stop instead of spinning, normal restart fills gaps, protected D2 state remains untouched, and no rebuild/recompute, parser-state correctness table, or Cortex-to-DB replay path is introduced.
